questions.stem: For CH2=CH–CH=CH2 in an approximately planar conformation, identify the continuous sequence of p orbitals and contrast it with CH2=CH–CH2–CH=CH2. Explain which structural feature interrupts that pathway in the second molecule.

answer.summary: Butadiene has four contiguous p-bearing centres; a central saturated CH2 in separated pentadiene interrupts this introductory pathway. This is not a proof of zero interaction of every quantum-mechanical kind.

reasoning_route.output: A four-site contiguous aligned p pathway.

questions.stem: A student assigns one hybridisation label to an entire molecule. Use propyne and allene to test this procedure and devise a more reliable local procedure. State the electron-domain information and orbital-consistency checks your procedure needs.

answer.summary: Count local sigma directions and lone pairs, conserve the valence basis, check residual p orientation and neighbouring compatibility, then qualify applicability. Propyne/allene classifications are atom-local.
